data.source_title: Increased Access to Professional Interpreters in the Hospital Improves Informed Consent for Patients with Limited English Proficiency
data.locator: Abstract, Key Results; Methods, Study Population
data.source_setting: Inpatients undergoing invasive cardiovascular, general surgery or orthopedic procedures at academic hospital; Chinese- and Spanish-speaking LEP patients
data.source_n: 152 LEP patients (84 pre, 68 post); post-implementation English comparison n=86
data.quantity: Adequate informed consent after bedside interpreter-phone implementation
data.value: 54% post vs 29% pre; p=0.001; adjusted OR 2.56 (95% CI 1.15-5.72)
data.source_evidence_basis: Adequacy required all three patient-reported elements: understanding reasons, risks, and all questions answered.
data.limitations: Prospective nonrandomized pre-post study; self-reported consent and propensity adjustment cannot eliminate confounding; intervention improved but did not erase disparity (post LEP vs English aOR 0.38).
data.inferred_scenario_use: For procedures, include access to a qualified interpreter and understanding of rationale/risks/questions in consent pathway; do not treat language group as a persona or prediction.
